post.summary: Exchange a code or refresh a connected app's key
post.description: Exchanges the authorization code and its PKCE verifier (S256) for an access token, the connected app's key, good for 1 hour, with a refresh token, or rotates the refresh token for a new pair. The code must be exchanged within 60 seconds of the person approving. The grant never widens past what was approved on the consent page, and a refresh token used twice ends the connection it belongs to.

post.description: Switches Database, Files (storage), Mail, Logs or Auth on for the environment. Workspace Admins only, with the product’s write scope, and the workspace must be entitled to the product (402 PRODUCT_ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED). The body is {} or, for Database only, {"engine":"sqlite"} or {"engine":"postgres"}: {} means SQLite, and an engine for any other product is 400. While the environment’s database (not deleted) uses the other engine the answer is 409 DATABASE_ENGINE_FIXED. The answer is 202 with the unfinished operation (follow it at Location), or 200 once it succeeded or failed; accepted is not done, and your app’s calls are refused until the operation succeeds. Each accepted request advances desiredRevision and supersedes an older unfinished operation of the same product. The same Idempotency-Key answers the same operation and never revives a superseded one; a different request under it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. 409 PRODUCT_OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS while a deletion of the product is still running, 409 PRODUCT_ARCHIVED while its data is archived for non-payment, 403 ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE where this stage does not serve the environment, 404 for an unknown product. Auth is the switch for sign-in: while it is off, no app address serves sign-in and switching sign-in on for one is refused (409 PRODUCT_DISABLED); each app keeps its own choice. Auth takes enable and disable only.

post.summary: Switch sign-in on for an app address
post.description: Switches sign-in on for one app address (origin) of the environment, so MDRN serves the sign-in pages there and tells your backend who is signed in. Workspace Admins only, with a credential that reaches the environment, and Auth must be on for the environment (409 PRODUCT_DISABLED). MDRN must already serve an active release of this project and environment at the address: an address MDRN does not serve is 404, one of another project, workspace or environment, or an inactive release, is 403. The answer is 200 with the activation once it succeeded, or with the failed operation; 202 with the unfinished operation otherwise (follow it at Location). The same Idempotency-Key with the same origin, project and environment answers the same operation; other input under it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. While the operation is retried, your credential, the Admin membership and the address's ownership are checked again.
post.x-mdrn-notes: Deploy is asked who serves the hostname now. Cookie mutations additionally require exact Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Scheduled retries recheck the initiating credential, current Admin membership and hostname ownership.

put.summary: Connect a repository and branch to a service
put.description: Connects serviceId to repositoryId in installationId, on branch or the repository's default branch, and builds what the branch holds now; from then on every push to the branch builds the commit at its head and, when the build succeeds, releases it. Only a repository the installation lists (one you could read when you authorized) can be connected; any other answers 404 NOT_FOUND. A branch with no commit yet, or a repository GitHub refuses MDRN, is not retried: the connection's problem says so until a later push or a reconnect clears it. The repository is held by its numeric identifier, so renaming it does not break the connection. One service deploys one repository and one branch; connecting another replaces the connection. One repository may feed several services, and a push builds each of them.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Scoped to the token, the project and environment, the method and the path. Send the same key when you retry the same change.

repository.description: Ignored; accepted for older callers. The name is the one GitHub gave when you authorized.

branch.description: A branch name git allows, of letters, digits and ._-/ (no .., no empty or dot-led component, no leading or trailing /, no .lock ending, no @{). Defaults to the default branch of the repository as GitHub gave it at authorization.

get.description: Names and settings only (secret, build, when each was last set), 100 per page. A value is never returned, for a secret or a plain variable.

put.summary: Set a variable on a service
put.description: Writes value under name, as a secret unless secret is false, and for the service's builds too when build is true; the value is never returned again. A name beginning with MDRN_ is refused, because that is where your app's product credentials live. If a release is serving, its artifact is published again so the change reaches the running app; deploymentId names that release. A release still in flight is replaced by that publication (superseded), so a missing variable can be fixed at once, unless it has already started on its database migrations or applied some: then the change answers 409 CONFLICT and changes nothing, because the serving code may not run on the database that release left; send it again once that release is live or has ended.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Scoped to the token, the project and environment, the method and the path. Send the same key when you retry the same change.

delete.summary: Remove a variable from a service
delete.description: Removes the variable and publishes the serving artifact again so the running app stops receiving it; deploymentId names that release, or null when nothing was serving. A release still in flight is replaced by that publication (superseded), unless it has already started on its database migrations or applied some: then the change answers 409 CONFLICT and changes nothing, because the serving code may not run on the database that release left; send it again once that release is live or has ended.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

post.description: Declares what you will upload for serviceId: a worker_bundle (a built bundle, published with POST /v1/deploy/deployments) or a source_archive (a directory to build with POST /v1/deploy/builds), its size in bytes and its SHA-256. Answers the URL, method and headers to send the bytes with, and when they expire. A worker_bundle is at most 32 MiB (33554432 bytes); a source_archive at most 95 MB (95000000 bytes), because our network refuses a larger request body. A larger declaration answers 413 UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE before any byte is sent; for a source archive, leave out node_modules, build output and .git, since the build installs dependencies itself.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Scoped to the token, the project and environment, the method and the path. Send the same key when you retry the same change.

expiresAt.description: Unix timestamp in seconds; the upload URL and its Authorization header expire 15 minutes after this answer.

put.description: Send the exact bytes whose size and SHA-256 you declared, with the Authorization header the upload answered and nothing else: no management token and no project or environment headers. Sending the same bytes again is safe.

post.description: Starts a build of sourceId for serviceId and answers 202 with the build and the URL of its log. The build runs in its own build container, started for this build alone. It needs no configuration file: its settings are the repository's own, read from an optional mdrn.jsonc at its root (comments allowed; an unknown key stops the build): rootDirectory, entry, buildCommand and testCommand, readinessPath, migrations (a directory of numbered .sql files) and output. A command naming an npm script runs that script; any other command runs as a shell line in the build container. Without output, MDRN bundles JavaScript or TypeScript from the entry point, found from the package manifest or where applications usually keep it. With output, the build produced the bundle and MDRN publishes that directory as it is: JavaScript, WebAssembly (Rust, Go, C, Zig) and Python modules, starting at entry or a conventional name, with a Python app's vendored python_modules. Rust, Go and Python toolchains are in the container. Without a testCommand nothing is tested. A successful build registers the artifact and makes an ordinary deployment, which goes through migration, readiness and activation like any other. One build at a time per service: starting another answers 409 CONFLICT. Source archives are kept for 30 days; building one after that answers 409 CONFLICT asking for the commit to be pushed or the source uploaded again. Build time past the 7 CPU-hours included each month is charged per CPU-hour, not refused; a build is refused while the workspace has no current plan (402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED), has an unpaid usage charge (402 PAYMENT_OVERDUE), or is at its spending cap where an Admin chose to stop builds (402 SPENDING_CAP_REACHED).
post.x-mdrn-notes: MDRN owns the runtime date. Toolchains in the build image: worker-build for Rust, TinyGo for Go, uv and pywrangler for Python. Product grants are issued at build creation, with the caller's credential, for the deployment the build will create; publication, supersession and activation are unchanged.

post.summary: Publish an artifact as a new release
post.description: Publishes artifactId (an uploaded bundle, or what a build produced) as a new deployment of serviceId and answers 202 with the deployment and the operation to follow. Refused while the workspace has no current plan (402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED), has an unpaid usage charge (402 PAYMENT_OVERDUE) or is at the spending cap where deploys stop (402 SPENDING_CAP_REACHED). An interrupted publication resumes on its own; repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same deployment. A bundle that carries migrations has them applied to the environment's Database before anything is published, each file as one transaction; a failing file fails the deployment with MIGRATION_FAILED, the files before it stay applied, and the previous release keeps serving. A bundle the runtime refuses for something in it (a module it imports that is not there, too much CPU while starting, its size, an unknown runtime flag, no handler, an exception at startup) fails the deployment at once with RELEASE_REFUSED, without retrying, and its log says what to change; the previous release keeps serving. Any earlier artifact of the service that is still kept can be published again as a new release, which is how you roll back; it answers 409 CONFLICT when the database already has migrations that artifact does not include. The newest ten releases of a service keep their bundle; an older one answers 409 CONFLICT until it is uploaded or built again.
post.x-mdrn-notes: The deployment and idempotency receipt are durable before acceptance. Each migration file is recorded in the database's own ledger.

post.summary: Add a custom domain to a service
post.description: Adds hostname to serviceId and answers the domain with the DNS records it needs. Nothing routes until our network reports the hostname active, and that is believed only once the workspace's ownership TXT record (ownershipChallenge, at _mdrn-challenge.<hostname>) has been seen in the hostname's DNS, when it was added or by a later check: until then the domain stays ownership_pending and lists that record as required. One custom domain per service. Apex domains work when the DNS host flattens CNAMEs; wildcards do not. Custom domains are served in production only; elsewhere this answers 409 CUSTOM_DOMAINS_UNAVAILABLE. Five hostnames are included per workspace. Beyond that each costs $0.15 per month and is charged for the days it serves: each day counts the most charged hostnames that served at any moment of it, so one waiting for its records, one that failed or one whose DNS moved away costs nothing. Adding one beyond the included ones without acceptCharge answers 402 DOMAIN_CHARGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with the quota and price; send that price back in acceptCharge to add it. A price that is not current answers 409 DOMAIN_CHARGE_CHANGED. A hostname another workspace holds answers 409 DOMAIN_CLAIMED with the ownership TXT record to add; with that record in the hostname's DNS, the same request removes the other claim and adds this one. A hostname nobody holds whose DNS already points to MDRN (it would serve at once) answers 409 DOMAIN_OWNERSHIP_REQUIRED with the same record; add it, then add the hostname again. A hostname never seen verified 7 days after it was added is released; one that was verified stays with its workspace even if its certificate renewal or DNS later fails.
post.x-mdrn-notes: ADR-63: a verified hostname stays with its workspace. Serving days come from custom_hostname_serving; billable_days counts each UTC day's peak beyond the included ones.

get.summary: Search the project environment’s application logs
get.description: Searches the logs of every service in the environment, or of one with service, newest first, in the window from and to name (the last hour when omitted). Requests, responses and exceptions are always returned; console lines below the capture level are not. level selects console lines and exceptions by level, as a comma-separated list of debug, log, info, warn and error (anything else answers 400); requests are returned whatever it is. q is at most 256 characters and matches text, without regard to case, in the items as they are answered, redacted and without anything a search leaves out, so it never matches a captured header. It is matched against the text a person reads, as it was written rather than as JSON escapes it: the message, the data logged beside it (its values, at any depth), the stack and the files a mapped stack names, the path, the service name, the request, invocation, correlation and trace IDs, numbers logged in the data (except under a name for a time: t, ts, or one holding time or date, or ending in At or _at) and the response status; never a field name, any other number, the kind, the level or the cursor. A page searched for text can hold fewer than 100 items while nextCursor goes on. Data logged beside a message is returned with it. Messages, paths, data and stacks are redacted: credential-named fields, bearer and basic credentials, cookie headers, credential-named key=value pairs and JSON members, and JSON Web Tokens. About the last six and a half days come from our network within seconds; older logs, up to the retention setting, come from the project archive, which fills within about five minutes. A page holds at most 100 items; a millisecond holding more than 100 recent items shows the first 100 of them. Pages walk the recent days newest first, then the archive newest object first: each archive page is newest first, and an object holds a few minutes of invocations, so neighbouring archive pages can overlap in time by that much. Where the walk passes from recent logs to the archive is fixed by its first page and carried in every cursor, so nothing is shown twice however long the walk takes. A walk is bound to its search (from and to as sent, level, q, service) and to the capture level and retention its first page read: a cursor sent with anything else, or after either setting changed, answers 400, and the search starts again without it, so a changed setting never makes a walk pass items over or show them twice. The window’s start as retention clamped it is carried in the cursor, so it does not move with the clock while the walk goes on. Once Logs is deleted for the environment, searches answer 403 PRODUCT_DISABLED until it is enabled again; a disabled Logs stays searchable until what it kept ages out. Every search counts as a read in Logs usage, in the UTC hour it ran.

AppSession.name: __Host-mdrn_app
AppSession.description: Opaque host-only application session cookie; Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain. Validated against private D1 with revocation and expiry checks. Browser JavaScript receives no service JWT or separate refresh token. Grants current-user Identity operations only, never product data.

UserBearer.description: The short-lived identity token (at most 5 minutes) the Proxy hands the app backend as x-mdrn-identity-token for a signed-in visitor. Accepted only on the current-user /v1/auth/me routes, which the backend calls through MDRN_PRODUCTS; never on product data routes and never an administrative key.

GitHubSignature.description: Provider signature of raw request; validate installation and replay identity.

StripeSignature.description: Provider raw-body signature/timestamp; use trusted endpoint secret and server-side customer mapping.

Maps are kept privately and never served or returned; embedded source text (sourcesContent) is removed before the bundle is published. Uncaught exceptions are mapped back to your source in the logs, after the fact; logged stack strings, WebAssembly and Python are not.

quantity.description: Null while a measurement is unknown.

url.description: Where delivery notifications go: https on the default port, without credentials or fragment, on a public DNS name of your own or on the project's own app address. A new URL moves the webhook and notifications still waiting follow it; null stops it and gives those up.

rotateKey.description: Replace the signing key. The answer carries the new key and the old one stops verifying at once; a rotation retried with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same key.

signingKey.description: The webhook's signing key, on the answer that first sets the webhook and on a rotation (or its retry) only. Store it before configuring the receiver.

origin.description: The app's https address exactly: no path, port, credentials or trailing slash. MDRN must already serve an active release of this project and environment there.

enabled.description: Whether sign-in is switched on for this address. It is served only while Auth is also on for the environment.

desiredRevision.description: Rises with every accepted request for the product.

observedState.description: The state the product last reported.

productionEnvironmentId.description: The id of its Production environment.

email.description: The address you signed in with; null when the sign-in carried none.

grants.description: One per workspace the credential reaches.

billingConfigured.description: Whether this stage takes payment, so the console can start the plan at checkout; where it does not, an account without a plan waits for one granted by hand.

version.description: The version of the terms the account agreed to (the current one when it is among them, else the latest), as a YYYY-MM-DD date; null before any agreement.

agreedAt.description: When that agreement was recorded, as a Unix time; null before any agreement.

current.description: Whether the account has agreed to the current version. Until it has, every console request but this read, agreeing and writing to support answers 403 TERMS_NOT_AGREED; tokens and connected apps are not held.

scopes.description: The scopes the credential holds in this workspace.

projectIds.description: The ones the credential is limited to; null for all of them, an empty array for none.

environmentIds.description: The ones the credential is limited to; null for all of them, an empty array for none.
